A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HyperAdapt work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and Appendix A are readable and support reliable matching across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original HyperAdapt fine-tuning results on GLUE, arithmetic reasoning, and commonsense reasoning, plus empirical update-rank analysis.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds reasoning-trace fine-tuning outcomes, singular-value analyses, and a learning-rate sensitivity experiment.

M1.justification: Both versions use W'=AW0B with identity-initialized diagonal scaling matrices, n+m trainable parameters, and precomputable adapted weights. Listing 1 is unchanged; the revised GLUE target layers concern experimental configuration.

E1.justification: Section 5.4 adds S1 reasoning-trace fine-tuning and MATH500 evaluation, introducing a distinct low-data, long-context scenario. GSM8K is additionally evaluated under this regime. Existing GLUE, Math10K, and Commonsense170K coverage remains.

E2.justification: GLUE Table 1 adds evaluated DoRA and VeRA rows; v1 mentioned VeRA in the caption but contained no corresponding row. Arithmetic Table 2 removes BoFT comparisons for Llama-3-8B and Qwen-2.5-7B. Other retained comparator memberships are unchanged.

E3.justification: GLUE adaptation targets change from Q/K/V/O to Q/V, and the commonsense batch size changes from 128 to 256 in Appendix A. The new reasoning-trace experiment uses a 16,384-token limit, batch size 64, five epochs, and training on traces and solutions excluding questions. The PDFs do not establish whether retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained normalized-rank heatmap, v2 adds query/value singular-value spectra for two models and two training datasets in Figure 4. Section 6.1 and Figure 5 introduce a six-learning-rate sweep using Math10K training and GSM8K evaluation, substantially expanding diagnostic and sensitivity analyses.

E5.justification: Section 5.1 broadens the explicit five-seed statement from HyperAdapt to all GLUE methods. This changes disclosed run coverage without establishing additional runs for retained results. Mean-and-standard-deviation reporting otherwise continues.

E6.justification: HyperAdapt's GLUE parameter count changes from 0.2M to 0.1M and its average from 86.4 to 86.0 under revised target-layer settings, so this is not a same-setting performance decline. Baseline result entries are added and removed. New S1 results report 89.0 on GSM8K and 64.0 on MATH500, alongside new spectral and sensitivity results. Retained arithmetic and commonsense table values are unchanged.

T1.justification: Lemma 1 retains the bound rank(ΔW) ≤ min{2 rank(W0), n, m} and the same proof. The normalized-rank definition and 10^-2 singular-value threshold are unchanged; restatement and equation numbering do not introduce new mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the claims of high-rank adaptation with n+m parameters, competitive performance, and no additional inference latency. The added experiments support these existing claims without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of the spectral and reasoning-trace results, including criticism of aggressive rank reduction in the new setting. Section 6.1 introduces learning-rate guidance and qualifications about extreme rates. The limitations concerning Transformer language models and dependence on pretraining remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A adds DoRA/VeRA GLUE hyperparameters and reasoning-trace training and decoding settings, including a 1,024-token generation cap. The text newly discloses the frozen GLUE classifier head and TRL usage, and the acknowledgements identify the DeltaAI computing system.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for S1, Gemini thinking traces, MATH500, and TRL: Muennighoff et al., Google, Lightman et al., and von Werra et al. The related-work discussion and positioning relative to existing PEFT methods remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: Local editing removes duplicated initialization prose, corrects the Theorem 1 reference to Lemma 1, and standardizes terminology and model names. New experiment and analysis subsections, appendix headings, and acknowledgements extend the otherwise retained narrative structure.

P2.justification: v2 adds the multipanel spectral Figure 4, sensitivity Figure 5, reasoning-results Table 4, and associated hyperparameter table. It expands GLUE tables, redraws the rank heatmap labels and grid, adds table highlighting and colored frozen-parameter counts, and rearranges appendix tables. Figure 4 introduces a substantive display inconsistency: its legend labels the abruptly collapsing curves HyperAdapt, contrary to its caption.

improvement.justification: The added GLUE comparisons, reasoning-trace evaluation, and learning-rate study provide useful validation and practical guidance beyond v1, supported by additional implementation details. The net gain is limited by Figure 4's conflicting method attribution, retained discussion of removed BoFT results, and unexplained revisions to existing experimental settings.
